Guide // Operating Manual

Every tool runs entirely in your browser. Nothing is uploaded. Pick a tab, follow the steps, and watch the shared Activity Log at the bottom for live status from whichever tool is running.

01 Media Converter

  1. Click Load Engine (the first load fetches FFmpeg.wasm and may take a moment).
  2. Drop a file (audio or video) onto the drop zone.
  3. Choose an output format and quality preset.
  4. Click Convert, then download the result.

Runs FFmpeg.wasm inside a Web Worker. Some formats and codecs are experimental in wasm builds; if one fails, try MP4 or WebM for video and WAV, MP3, AAC or FLAC for audio (the log shows the exact error).

Advanced controls

  • Bitrate Compression quality for MP3/AAC/Opus/Vorbis. Higher = bigger file.
  • Sample rate Resamples audio. Common: 44100 (music), 48000 (video).
  • Channels Downmix or force stereo. Mono reduces size.
  • FPS Video frame rate. Higher = smoother but heavier.
  • Scale Resize video. Use -1 to keep aspect ratio (e.g. 1280:-1).
  • Codec Video encoder. Availability depends on the wasm build.
  • CRF Quality knob (H.264/VP9). Lower = better quality, bigger file. Typical 18–28.
  • GIF FPS / scale Trade animation smoothness against file size.

02 Extract

  1. Run the local helper on your own machine: python3 media-helper/server.py (needs yt-dlp and ffmpeg installed).
  2. Wait for the status dot to turn green, or click Retry.
  3. Paste a media URL. Optionally click Inspect to preview title and duration.
  4. Click Get Audio (the default) or Get Video.
  5. Send the result straight to Transform or Converter, or download it.

The helper is a tiny wrapper around yt-dlp that runs on your machine (or your own VPS), so the download never passes through a third-party server. The web page just drives it — like the way you supply your own model to the Transcribe tool.

Notes

  • Local Binds to 127.0.0.1:8765 by default. See media-helper/README.md for Docker / VPS setup.
  • Scope Public, non-DRM media only. It cannot and does not decrypt paid or protected streams.
  • Audio-first Grabs bestaudio by default (fast, small, no video pulled); switch to video when you need the picture.
  • Upkeep Keep the helper current with pip install -U yt-dlp — sites change often.

03 Piano Transcription

  1. Download the pretrained ONNX model using the button in the tool.
  2. Load the model by dropping the .onnx file onto the model area (or click to choose).
  3. Load a piano audio file (mono or stereo, any sample rate).
  4. Click Run Transcription and wait (audio is resampled to 16 kHz and split into overlapping chunks).
  5. When finished, click Download MIDI to save the transcription, including sustain pedal (CC64) events.

Model details

  • Model CRNN piano transcription with onset/offset regression and a separate pedal head. Uses 10 s segments with 5 s overlap and overlap-stitching.
  • Source Kong, Li, Song, Wan, Wang (2020), “High-resolution Piano Transcription with Pedals by Regressing Onsets and Offsets Times” (arXiv:2010.01815).
  • Checkpoint Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.4034264, exported to ONNX.
  • License Model weights CC-BY 4.0 (attribution required); this wrapper is MIT.

04 Loudness & Masking Analyzer

  1. Load an audio file (and optionally a reference track).
  2. Click Analyze to compute loudness metrics and masking heatmaps.

Computes BS.1770-5 loudness, Zwicker loudness, and MPEG-1 Psychoacoustic Model 1 masking with persistent-mask and margin heatmaps.

Accuracy notes

  • BS.1770-5 Tested, accurate to the 2nd decimal.
  • Zwicker / MPEG Adaptations for reference only; not a guaranteed faithful replication of the original experiments, standards or publications.
  • Platform penalties References only; we do not have direct access to each platform's algorithm.

05 Transform

  1. Load audio — drop a file, or send one over from the Extract tab.
  2. Build a chain (up to 6 stages): Pitch, Stretch, Reverse, Vocode. Reorder with the ↑/↓ buttons.
  3. Tune each stage, then click Render (runs offline in a worker).
  4. Compare the before / after spectrograms, play the result, then download the WAV or send it to Converter.

The goal is to reshape a sound while keeping it recognizable: the phase and spectrum can change completely, but the pitch contour, rhythm and intelligibility survive. Runs entirely on Web Audio.

Transforms

  • Pitch Shifts pitch without changing duration (phase vocoder + resample). Preserve formants keeps voices natural instead of chipmunked.
  • Stretch Changes duration without changing pitch. Preserve transients keeps drums and consonants sharp.
  • Reverse Plays the audio backwards. No parameters.
  • Vocode Imposes the content's band envelopes on an internal synth carrier (saw / pulse / noise). Words and melody stay intelligible while the timbre is replaced.

06 Transfer

  1. On the sending device, open Send and click Create transfer code. A 6-digit code and a QR appear.
  2. On the receiving device, open Receive and type the code — or just scan the QR with its camera, which opens this page straight to the transfer.
  3. Both devices show a security-check row of 5 symbols. Confirm they match, then the sender clicks Symbols match — continue.
  4. (Optional, recommended) On the receiver, click Choose destination folder to stream straight to disk.
  5. On the sender, choose files, choose a folder, or drag items onto the drop zone. Progress shows on both ends and in the Activity Log.

Files travel directly device-to-device over an encrypted WebRTC channel — they are never uploaded or stored. Only the 6-digit handshake passes through a tiny signaling broker, which never sees file names or contents. Keep the tab open on both devices.

Notes

  • Security check The 5 symbols are derived from the connection itself; if they differ on the two devices, someone may be intercepting — stop and retry.
  • Folders Folder sending and streaming-to-disk need desktop Chrome or Edge. Other browsers download each file individually to the Downloads folder.
  • Resume If a transfer is interrupted, reconnect with a new code and resend the same folder: files already fully written to the chosen destination are detected and skipped.
  • Networks A direct connection can fail on strict corporate/carrier networks (no relay fallback is used). Try a different network if it can't connect.
  • Codes Each code is single-use and expires after about 10 minutes.
